claims.claim: FR notice 2026-21447 describes an order (1) excluding IT products and services developed by Hangzhou DeepSeek and affiliates from federal civilian procurements and (2) removing DeepSeek, affiliate, and third-party products and services developed using DeepSeek implementations from civilian agency IT.
The notice was filed for public inspection on 2026-10-19 for publication on 2026-10-20 under docket DHS-2026-0628 and is signed by DHS General Counsel James H. Percival II.
The order's date is reported as July 24, 2026 (original release date) by CellCog and MeriTalk, while CyberScoop reports a June 26 letter.
41 U.S.C. 1323 assigns FASCSA order authority to DHS for civilian agencies, the Secretary of Defense for DoD and national security systems, and the DNI for the intelligence community and SCI systems.

FAR 52.204-30 defines reasonable inquiry as covering information in the entity's possession and excluding the need for an internal or third-party audit, with reporting within 3 business days and follow-up within 10.
Under FAR 52.204-30(b)(4), a FASCSA order issued after the solicitation date applies to a contract only if added by amendment or modification.
Judicial review of a FASCSA order lies exclusively in the D.C. Circuit on a petition filed within 60 days after the party is notified.
The first FASCSA order was issued by the DNI against Acronis AG in September 2025, covering the intelligence community.
FY2026 NDAA section 1532 bars DoD and DoD contractors from using covered AI developed by DeepSeek or High Flyer, effective about Jan 17, 2026.
NIST CAISI found DeepSeek R1-0528 agents 12 times more likely to follow malicious instructions and 94% jailbreak compliance versus 8% for U.S. reference models.
CrowdStrike tested raw open-source DeepSeek-R1 671B and found severe-vulnerability rates rising from 19% baseline to 27.2% with a Tibet trigger.
DeepSeek-R1 on Hugging Face lists 327 finetunes, 122 adapters, 70 quantizations, and 5 merges.
Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct lists 3,174 finetunes on Hugging Face versus 327 for DeepSeek-R1.
AWS's FedRAMP Bedrock model list does not include DeepSeek, while commercial Bedrock serves DeepSeek-R1 through US cross-region inference.
DeepSeek was the largest open-model author on OpenRouter with 14.37 trillion tokens over Nov 2024-Nov 2025, versus 5.59 trillion for Qwen.
Distillation detection from a student model alone is highly challenging; weight-lineage tests require white-box access.
Kimi K2's config declares the DeepseekV3ForCausalLM architecture.
Brookings counts $91.8B in potential value of federal AI contracts, of which DoD holds $90.7B (98.9%).
Perplexity announced DeepSeek V4 Pro hosted in the U.S. in Perplexity Computer in August 2026.
The DeepSeek-R1 weights and code are released under the MIT License, which permits distillation.
